food_summary: graphify (PyPI graphifyy 0.9.101, commit 8e6a6d2, Apache-2.0, ~60.7k lines of Python) builds a local tree-sitter code graph with query/path/explain/affected CLIs, an MCP server and a host skill. Retrieval is lexical substring+IDF plus graph traversal, not vectors, and per the wiki-duel judge it complements the OAW LLM wiki rather than replacing it. Ledger: 31 components, 13 excrete, 13 absorb, 5 hold. Excreted: the agent-steering and installer layer (always-on query-first router, silent uv/pip install, silent self-refresh of installed SKILL.md files, opt-in git hooks with job-escaping detached rebuilds, PreToolUse guards in shared settings.json, global CLAUDE.md registration with a confirmed H1-boundary bug that deletes user sections, the 48-50 KB skill package), ambient LLM egress including an unrestricted nested `claude -p`, the repo-controlled .graphify_python interpreter, the Write+Bash doc-extraction fan-out, the directory-sweeping wiki exporter, the save-result memory loop, and the MCP/PR tools. Absorbed as stdlib methods into existing OAW parts: a `path::Symbol` citation lint and a read-only reverse 'cites' lookup in wiki_sync.py, hash plus renderer-version staleness in wiki_sync.py, budget-fit reporting and 0/3/4 exit codes in context_hub.py, and a references/ remedy for the planned 24,000-byte gate in validate_skills.py. Absorbed into the planned catalog.py digestion pipeline: untrusted-source wrapping, reviewer read-coverage checks, rubric fingerprints, a hook-safety rubric, an installer round-trip check, credential-file flags and URL validation. Held for paid tests: graphify itself as a manual-only external code-map pack (pinned, project scope, GRAPHIFY_BACKEND=none, GRAPHIFY_NO_AUTO_REFRESH=1, no skill, no hooks, graphify-out/ gitignored), a stdlib code map, IDF ranking, query expansion and outcome-scored promotion. Nothing is installed. Absorbed items need deterministic tests under harness_check. Changes that affect behavior also need improvement.py A/B, and every OAW draft needs a goldfish review (D10). Status: parity, no improvement claimed.

components.name: Always-on CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md rule block
components.what: Marker section `## graphify` written into the project CLAUDE.md (graphify claude install / install --project) or AGENTS.md (codex install). It requires `graphify query` before the first grep, search or source-file read, says to copy that rule into every subagent prompt, limits raw reads to lines the graph located, and tells reviewers not to flag graph.json churn or suggest skipping the rebuild or its hooks. The AGENTS variant adds 'only skip graphify if the user explicitly says not to use it'.
components.reason: A second mandatory router, which OAW v2 removed on purpose. v2.0.0 also forbids shipping a mandatory nudge or graph memory. Copying the rule into every subagent prompt inflates EGM and goldfish prompts. The reviewer clause pre-empts judgement about the tool's own footprint. The verifier narrows it to graph.json PR diffs, but it still conflicts. Appending the block to OAW-managed CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md changes their managed hash, so doctor reports a modified managed file and the next framework update becomes a migration conflict.

components.name: Skill Step 1 silent install/upgrade
components.what: When `import graphify` fails, the skill runs `uv tool install --upgrade graphifyy` (unpinned) or `pip install graphifyy`. If that fails it retries with `--break-system-packages`. On success it prints nothing. The same block is in skill-codex.md and skill-windows.md.
components.reason: Breaks OAW's never-auto-install/upgrade/apply rule and D7, which requires consent before any install. An unpinned upgrade breaks pinned-SHA evidence, and --break-system-packages can modify the system Python. Verifier: it runs only when the import fails, and the system-packages retry is a fallback. That narrows the scope but does not add consent.

components.name: Silent self-refresh of installed SKILL.md files
components.what: After a package upgrade, every non-silent CLI run calls `_refresh_stale_skills` and `_refresh_v1_opencode_plugins`. That includes `graphify query`, which the router tells agents to run constantly. Together they re-copy SKILL.md and references/ for every user-scope platform and rewrite OpenCode plugin files. Only a SKILL.md.bak is kept. The opt-out is GRAPHIFY_NO_AUTO_REFRESH=1, and the behavior is disclosed only in the CHANGELOG.
components.reason: An auto-update channel for agent instructions. It contradicts OAW's rule that nothing applies itself and the v2 ban on a self-rewriting background component. It also voids catalog evidence pinned to a SHA, because the instructions the agent follows change without re-digestion.

components.name: graphify hook install (git hooks, merge driver, detached rebuilds)
components.what: An opt-in command. It installs post-commit, post-checkout, post-merge and post-rewrite hooks, registers a merge.graphify.* git-config driver that runs a pinned interpreter, and appends a line to the tracked .gitattributes. Each hook spawns a detached Python rebuild (start_new_session; on Windows with CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB) that logs to ~/.cache/graphify-rebuild.log. The agent-facing doc mentions only a post-commit hook and says 'No background process needed'.
components.reason: It creates background processes that can escape the parent's job object (agent sandbox or CI) and writes to git config, a tracked file and the home directory. Its documentation also contradicts the code. OAW ships no git hooks, its packaging allowlist rejects hooks, and v2 forbids background daemons. Verifier: the command is opt-in and not part of the default install, so excreting it costs the held code-map route nothing. The well-made hook craft is kept as rubric items in gf.hook-safety-rubric.

components.sources_agree: Digest (flag d), verifier (opt-in correction), goldfish-1 and goldfish-2 (major) agree. Wiki duel says never run `graphify hook install`.

components.name: PreToolUse hook-guard (Claude) and no-op hook-check (Codex)
components.what: `graphify claude install` and `install --project` merge two PreToolUse entries into the shared .claude/settings.json: Bash|Grep runs `hook-guard search` and Read|Glob runs `hook-guard read`, each with a 10s timeout. --strict or GRAPHIFY_HOOK_STRICT denies the first raw Read in each session. Outside --project the entry embeds the installing machine's absolute exe path in that usually-committed file. Codex gets a .codex/hooks.json `hook-check` entry with no timeout: it spawns a process on every Bash call and exits 0.
components.reason: It starts a Python process on the four most-used tools (about 170 ms warm by the project's own figure; Windows is unmeasured). Its nudges repeat the router, and strict mode can block harness_check and EGM flows. Claude gets runtime hooks while Codex gets prose only, which fails OAW's cross-host counterpart rule. A machine path committed to config breaks every other clone.

components.name: Global '# graphify' registration and its section-boundary bug
components.what: Default `graphify install` copies the skill to ~/.claude/skills (or ~/.codex/skills; on Windows the default is the 'windows' variant). Without asking, it adds an H1 `# graphify` block to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md or $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/CLAUDE.md. The block's section ends at the next line starting with '# '. A re-install or project uninstall therefore deletes every user `##` section written after the block, and an emptied file is unlinked. `graphify uninstall` never removes the global block.
components.reason: Three problems: unconsented user-global writes outside the project, a confirmed data-loss path in the user's CLAUDE.md, and a stale instruction left after uninstall. OAW keeps CLAUDE.md as a one-line @AGENTS.md import and protects existing content.

components.name: Ambient LLM backend auto-detection and claude -p fallback
components.what: Headless extract, label and cluster-only pick a provider from whatever keys are in the environment, in the order gemini, kimi, claude, openai, deepseek, azure, bedrock, ollama. They send it doc content or community member labels, which are code identifiers. With no key, labeling spawns `claude -p` using the local CLI's default model. The call passes no --tools, --allowedTools or --permission-mode, so it inherits the cwd's CLAUDE.md, skills and hooks. The skill tells the agent 'No other API keys are read' and uses Gemini preview automatically when a Gemini key is set.
components.reason: Data leaves the machine and money is spent without an explicit choice. The agent-facing skill makes a false claim. The nested agent is unconstrained and fed untrusted corpus text. OAW needs none of it: OAW tools make no model calls, and OAW's paid runner already pins tools, disallowed tools, setting sources, permission mode and a per-invocation budget. graphify's mitigations (stderr announcement, GRAPHIFY_BACKEND=none, --no-label) become mandatory settings in gf.code-map-external rather than being absorbed.

components.name: LLM doc-extraction pass (subagent fan-out)
components.what: For docs, PDFs and images, the skill forbids the agent from reading files itself. It dispatches about ceil(files/22) general-purpose subagents with Write and Bash, all running extraction-spec.md. Unlike llm.py's API path, that spec has no 'file content is untrusted' clause. It asks for aggressive INFERRED edges in deep mode and semantically_similar_to edges, leaves source_location null, and concatenates rationale fragments without their source or date.
components.reason: Bash-capable subagents read cloned repos, which opens an injection surface, and the spend is unbounded. The output also does not suit OAW decision notes: superseded and current rationale become indistinguishable and lose line provenance, whereas OAW keeps verbatim source text with ref, ID and date per source. The useful part, graphify's no-LLM markdown references layer, is absorbed through gf.code-citation-lint.

components.name: save-result / reflect work-memory loop
components.what: `graphify save-result` writes the user's verbatim question and the model's full answer into graphify-out/memory/*.md. detect() always re-ingests that directory, so the saved answers become graph nodes. reflect.py turns their outcomes into reflections/LESSONS.md for the next session to read.

components.name: Reverse lookup: which notes cite this code
components.what: `graphify affected <Symbol>` walks references, calls and imports edges in reverse to list what depends on a symbol, including the docs that cite it.

components.name: Refuse-to-guess exit codes
components.what: query, path and explain exit 0 for an answer, 3 for an ambiguous name (with candidates listed) and 4 for no match.
components.oaw_target: scripts/context_hub.py get and search (exit status and candidate listing) + tests/test_context_hub.py + docs/CLI_Reference.md
components.reason: OAW `get` returns 1 for a missing topic without suggesting candidates, and `search` exits 0 when nothing matches, so a script or agent cannot tell 'no match' from 'ambiguous'. Adopt distinct codes and list near candidates (case-insensitive or substring topic ids) instead of guessing. This changes the CLI contract, so the harness cli_check and the CLI reference must change in the same commit.

components.name: Content-hash plus renderer-version staleness
components.what: graphify namespaces its AST cache by package, schema and grammar version, and keys its semantic cache by content plus a normalized prompt fingerprint. A tool upgrade or an edited input therefore invalidates outputs deterministically.

components.reason: OAW lint flags a stale page only when a raw note's last_updated is newer than the page. An edit that forgets to bump the date, or a renderer change, goes unseen. Storing source hashes and the renderer version in the generated frontmatter lets lint report exactly 'raw changed since compile'. Only build_origin wiki_sync pages carry this frontmatter, so manual pages are untouched.

graphify/cache.py:141-163 (prompt_fingerprint normalizes CRLF and trailing whitespace)

claim_corrections: Revision 1 stored a per-source sha256 in frontmatter. context_hub get prints frontmatter in full, so full 64-hex hashes cost about 40 tokens per source; the proposal uses re-render comparison plus RENDERER_VERSION instead (short digests if per-source hashes are ever added).

components.name: Labelled, hash-stamped untrusted-data blocks with delimiter defanging

components.name: Reviewer read-coverage verification
components.what: Each extraction subagent reports the lines it read per file. The skill compares those counts with real file lengths, warns about short reads, and caches them as partial so they are retried. The Read tool truncates at 2000 lines without any error.

A source needs at least 2 distinct corroborations before it is 'preferred', and contested items and known dead ends get their own lists. Output is deterministic.

That pipeline is the digestion system, separate from eating this food. graphify still showed what it lacks: an untrusted-data wrapper, reviewer read-coverage checks, rubric fingerprints, a hook-safety rubric and an installer round-trip check.

Absorb order, all free and deterministic: gf.code-citation-lint, then gf.reverse-citation-lookup, gf.hash-staleness, gf.budget-fit-report and gf.ambiguity-exit-codes. Each goes through improvement.py propose with a concrete diff, gets a goldfish review as an OAW draft (D10) and passes harness_check. The per-version citation lists this repo as used_in for the changed files (D3).
No paid test has run. Every hold needs the owner's consent and a budget with an estimate first (D7).
revision_rule: Revision 2 (integration-resolved). Every component keeps its revision-1 fields as the historical record. Where a component has an 'after_integration' object, that object is canonical: its disposition, oaw_target, claim_corrections, missing_test and backlog fields supersede the revision-1 fields they restate. A split component lists its parts in after_integration.parts, and each part has its own disposition; counts_after_integration counts units (unsplit components plus parts), not components. Components with 'added_in_revision': 2 were added to give minor digest, verifier and goldfish items a disposition. Integration checked absorb components only; excrete components without an after_integration object are unchanged and each becomes a D3 not-adopted line through backlog PRE-08.
